newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SAC to buy 0.5 mln t/yr naphtha on spot/semi-term.
newsitem.headline: SAC to buy 0.5 mln t/yr naphtha on spot/semi-term.

text.p: Singapore Aromatics Company Pte (SAC) plans to cover 35 percent of its 1.5 million tonne per year naphtha feedstock requirements on the spot and semi-term basis, a company source said on Monday.
SAC began test runs at its new petrochemical complex early December and commercial production mid-January.

"Paraxylene production started January 15," a spokesman said. The complex which was designed to produce 350,000 tonnes of paraxylene and 96,000 tonnes of benzene annually, is slated for its formal inauguration in July, he said.

Paraxylene is used to manufacture purified terephthalic acid (PTA), a key component in the production of polyester. Benzene is used to make styrene monomer, a feedstock for plastics and synthethic rubber.
SAC has arrangements by which its shareholders offtake the production.

SAC is a joint venture made up by Exxon Chemical Singapore Private Limited with a 50 percent share, Amoco Chemical Holding Company with 40 percent and the remainder held by China American Singapore Company Private Ltd, an affiliate of Taiwanese China America Petrochemical Company (CAPCO), itself a joint venture between Amoco and state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp, a press statement said.
The six-month semi-term supply contract has already been concluded but details were private and confidential the source said.

The complex will take close to one million tonnes per year or 65 percent of its 0.7SG heavy, naphthenic and aromatic feedstock from Esso Singapore's 230,000 barrel-per-day refinery, also located at Pulau Ayer Chawan, an island off the south coast of Singapore.
Esso stopped in January sales of the up to three 25,000-30,000-tonne cargoes per month of heavy naphtha. It now only sells one cargo of light material of 0.66-67SG.
